<a id="s0-p1"></a>[0¶1] This document is the contract for a *measurement set*: a named, versioned file of measured machine costs (the scalar walk's per-byte cost and the costs and crossovers of the search-code kit's forms on one box) that a compile reads to choose among sound alternatives. It states the file format, the codes and the digest, the stamp an artifact carries, how a compile finds its set, the listing, the failures and the store. The design is `docs/design/measure_sets.md`, which is background and not normative.

<a id="s0-p2"></a>[0¶2] The promise that frames the rest: a set may change SPEED, never an ANSWER, never a GIVE-UP. Every reader of a set value chooses among options each of which is sound, so any set gives the same answers and the same give-ups. A quantity a set does not hold, or holds as `null`, is a skip, never a presumed value.

<a id="s1"></a>
## 1. Terms

| term | meaning |
|---|---|
| set | one file of §2's shape: a header, the method cards, the rows, the raw cells, and (for an envelope) its members |
| row | one measured, fitted or derived quantity, keyed by one canonical key (§2.3) |
| card | one quantity's METHOD: its dimensions, unit, subject regime and gate, copied into the set it was measured under |
| unit row | the row every relative value is relative to (`unit_key`), a `ratio` of value 1 |
| loaded set | the set a compile resolved (§5): the named one, else the build's default |
| consulted | a reader looked a key up in the loaded set, found or absent (§4) |

<a id="s2"></a>
## 2. The file

<a id="s2-p1"></a>[2¶1] A set is one text file in `table_contract.md`'s section shape (§2, §4): TAB-separated fields, LF line ends, `#` lines are comments, `#section NAME` at column 1 opens a section, and a section's header is its last `#` line before its first row. Every row carries exactly its header's field count. An empty line is skipped. A CR or NUL byte refuses the file.

<a id="s2-p2"></a>[2¶2] The sections are `header`, `cards`, `rows`, `cells` and `members`, and no other. Columns resolve by name; a column the tables below do not name is tolerated and not carried. A known column missing from a section that has a header refuses the file. A data row before the first `#section` refuses it.

<a id="s2-p3"></a>[2¶3] The derived views' sections (`decoded`, `item`, `readers`, `stale`, `sets`) are never an input: a file carrying one is refused by name (§7).

<a id="s2-1"></a>
### 2.1 The header

<a id="s2-1-p1"></a>[2.1¶1] Section `header` has the columns `key` and `value`, one row per key, each key at most once. The keys, in the canonical writer's order (R marks a key that must be present and non-empty):

| key | R | value |
|---|---|---|
| `format` | R | `1` |
| `id` | R | the set's name, `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*` |
| `rev` | R | its revision, a positive decimal |
| `class` | R | the ISA level and tuning class it was measured for |
| `isa` | | the measuring box's ISA features (provenance) |
| `tier` | R | `scratch`, `official`, `local` or `synthetic` |
| `composite` | R | `1` for an envelope over member sets, else `0` |
| `members` | | an envelope's members as `id@rev:digest` items, `;`-joined; empty for a measured set |
| `unit_key` | R | the key of the unit row |
| `method` | R | the method cards' `owner-name@ver` |
| `run`, `box`, `compiler`, `libc`, `code_commit`, `counters` | | provenance |
| `partial` | | `1` when only some groups passed their gates, else `0` or empty |
| `rows` | R | the number of rows in section `rows` |
| `values_digest` | R | §3.3's digest, 16 lowercase hex |

<a id="s2-1-p2"></a>[2.1¶2] An unknown header key refuses the file.

<a id="s2-2"></a>
### 2.2 The tables

<a id="s2-2-p1"></a>[2.2¶1] The columns of the four tables, in the canonical writer's order:

| section | columns |
|---|---|
| `cards` | `owner quantity ver dims unit subject lengths launches rounds aa_rule gate_e6 env deps` |
| `rows` | `key unit value_e6 abs_ns_e6 noise_e6 n status derivation inputs deps tags source` |
| `cells` | `cell group arm length launch round ns_e6` |
| `members` | `member unit_key unit_abs_ns_e6 box` |

<a id="s2-2-p2"></a>[2.2¶2] A card's `dims` lists the quantity's dimension names, `;`-joined; `-` or empty is none. A card's `owner` is `kit` or `pcrec`. A set holds at most one card per `owner.quantity`.

<a id="s2-2-p3"></a>[2.2¶3] In `rows`, `value_e6` is the value times 10^6 as a decimal integer in its one spelling (no `+`, no leading zero, no `-0`); it is empty exactly on a `null` row. `derivation` is `-` or empty on a `measured` or `null` row and names a §3.2 derivation on a `derived` or `fitted` row. `inputs` is `-`, empty, or `;`-joined row keys and cell ids of this set; only a `derived` or `fitted` row names inputs. The other columns are provenance and display, carried as text.

<a id="s2-2-p4"></a>[2.2¶4] A cell id appears at most once. `composite` is `1` exactly when `members` (the header key) is non-empty and section `members` has rows.

<a id="s2-3"></a>
### 2.3 The key

<a id="s2-3-p1"></a>[2.3¶1] A row's key is one canonical string:

```
key      := owner "." quantity { "." token }
owner    := "kit" | "pcrec"
quantity := [a-z][a-z0-9_]*
token    := [A-Za-z0-9_+-]+ , and not the single character "-"
```

<a id="s2-3-p2"></a>[2.3¶2] The tokens are the quantity's dimension values in the order its card's `dims` declares, so a key's token count equals its card's dimension count. A key is unique within a set. The format defines no placeholder token and reads no owner's vocabulary: `kit.beta.V1.ANY.r2e0c0` is a key of `kit`'s `beta` under a card whose `dims` is `form;kind;shape`, whatever `ANY` means to the kit.

<a id="s3"></a>
## 3. Values, codes and the digest

<a id="s3-1"></a>
### 3.1 The codes

<a id="s3-1-p1"></a>[3.1¶1] A row's unit and status are each one of a closed list with a fixed byte, which the digest hashes. `0x00` is never assigned, and a new unit or status is a new row with a new byte, never a reuse:

| unit | byte | | status | byte |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ratio` | `0x01` | | `measured` | `0x01` |
| `walkbytes` | `0x02` | | `fitted` | `0x02` |
| `bytes` | `0x03` | | `derived` | `0x03` |
| `count` | `0x04` | | `null` | `0x04` |

<a id="s3-1-p2"></a>[3.1¶2] The unit row is a `ratio` whose `value_e6` is `1000000`; exactly one row is named by `unit_key`.

<a id="s3-2"></a>
### 3.2 The derivations

<a id="s3-2-p1"></a>[3.2¶1] The closed list of derivations a `derived` or `fitted` row may name:

| derivation | value |
|---|---|
| `ratio` | a / b |
| `ratio-complement` | 1 − a / b |
| `diff` | a − b |
| `cross-lin` | (F_b − F_a) / (β_a − β_b), in bytes |
| `step` | a form's block width |
| `min`, `max` | of the inputs |
| `interp-log2` | linear in log2 of the abscissa between the two bracketing cells where the measured effect changes sign |
| `env-max`, `env-min` | over an envelope's members |

<a id="s3-2-p2"></a>[3.2¶2] A derived or fitted row with a `null` input is `null`. A value a selection reads is the row's `value_e6` as stored; no reader recomputes a derivation.

<a id="s3-3"></a>
### 3.3 The values digest

<a id="s3-3-p1"></a>[3.3¶1] `values_digest` is FNV-1a-64 over the 13 bytes `pcrec-meas-1` and its terminating NUL, then, for each row in canonical order (a bytewise sort of the keys), the key's bytes, a NUL, the unit byte, the status byte and `value_e6` as a little-endian int64 (`INT64_MIN` for an empty value), written as 16 lowercase hex. It covers no provenance column, card, cell or member, so the same values from any provenance give the same digest.

<a id="s3-3-p2"></a>[3.3¶2] The header's `values_digest` must equal the digest of the rows, and `rows` must equal their count; a file where either differs is refused.

<a id="s4"></a>
## 4. The stamp: `<PREFIX>_MEASURES` and `rx_info.measures`

<a id="s4-p1"></a>[4¶1] Every artifact carries `<PREFIX>_MEASURES` beside `<PREFIX>_FINDINGS`, mirrored byte for byte by `rx_info.measures` (`match_api.md` §6.3.10¶12, §6¶14a):

```c
#define RX_MEASURES "zen4-grid1@1:13a6536315af1520"   /* consulted */
#define RX_MEASURES ""                                /* nothing consulted */
```

<a id="s4-p2"></a>[4¶2] The value is `id@rev:values_digest` of the LOADED set when a reader consulted it, and the empty string otherwise. A reader is pcrec's own (none exists today) or the search-code kit's, which reports whether any of its rows resolved a key against the set, found or absent. A key looked up and not found still consults: the artifact depends on the set's not holding it.

<a id="s4-p3"></a>[4¶3] The stamp is written after every reader has run. It lists the set if ANY attempt of the compile consulted it, a discarded retry attempt included, and on a compound if P's compile or any part's compile consulted it. P and its parts read one set (§5¶8), so the value names that set whichever of them consulted.

<a id="s4-p4"></a>[4¶4] With the stamp empty, the artifact's bytes are the same under every set. No kit row reads a set key today, so every artifact's stamp is `""`.

<a id="s4-p5"></a>[4¶5] The set's id is plain text in the artifact; name sets neutrally.

<a id="s5"></a>
## 5. Loading: which set a compile reads

<a id="s5-p1"></a>[5¶1] **Spelling.** `--measures X` (or `--measures=X`), the `.rxt` config line `measures X` (`rxt_format.md`), and the library's `pcrec_options.measures` (`match_api.md` §8.2¶7b) take one value. A value that is a legal set name, optionally followed by `@` and a revision (decimal, no leading zero), is a NAME; anything else is a FILE. No file is probed to decide: `./zen4-grid1` is a FILE and `zen4-grid1` a NAME in every directory.

<a id="s5-p2"></a>[5¶2] **A NAME** is looked up in two stops, in order: `DIR/<name>.measures.tsv` for each `-I DIR` (`pcrec_options.measures_dirs`), the directory entry matched exactly; then the sets built into the binary (§8). An `-I` file whose header `id` is not NAME refuses the compile, as does one whose `rev` differs from a pinned `NAME@REV`. A NAME without `@REV` names the store's latest revision. A NAME found nowhere refuses, naming the stops searched.

<a id="s5-p3"></a>[5¶3] **A FILE** is read directly.

<a id="s5-p4"></a>[5¶4] **No shadowing.** A set read from a file (an `-I` file or a FILE value) whose (`id`, `rev`) is a committed set must have that set's `values_digest`, and one whose `id` is committed under another revision only is refused. So a stamp naming `id@rev` always names the values the store holds.

<a id="s5-p5"></a>[5¶5] **Precedence.** Fill-only, as `--analysis`: a target whose config names `measures` gets that set, and `--measures` names the set for targets whose configs name none. Where both are given and differ, the file's value wins and a note names both. A `pcrec` config line carrying `--measures` is refused.

<a id="s5-p6"></a>[5¶6] **The default.** A compile that names no set reads the build's default for its class. Today there is one class, `idk` (a compile that declares none), and its default is the latest committed set: `zen4-grid1@1`, measured on one box.

<a id="s5-p7"></a>[5¶7] Loading moves no artifact byte: only a CONSULTED set is stamped (§4).

<a id="s5-p8"></a>[5¶8] **A compound's parts.** Each part of a compound (`match_api.md` §3.7) reads the set P's compile loaded: the same document, so the same `id@rev` and values. A part does not load a set of its own, so no file, `-I` stop or default can give it a different one.

<a id="s6"></a>
## 6. The listing: `--list-measurements`

<a id="s6-p1"></a>[6¶1] `--list-measurements` (no value) prints section `sets`, one row per committed set: `id rev class box tier composite method default_for rows null_rows values_digest source`. `default_for` is the class it is the default of, or empty.

<a id="s6-p2"></a>[6¶2] `--list-measurements=X` (X a NAME, NAME@REV or FILE, resolved by §5¶1-¶4 with `-I`) prints the set's CANONICAL view: its five sections in §2's order, the header keys in §2.1's order (an absent key as an empty value), the rows in canonical key order, the cards, cells and members in bytewise order of their fields, one fixed first comment line and no other comment. The canonical view of a set IS a loadable set with the same digest, and the canonical view of a canonical view is itself, byte for byte. Every committed set file equals its own canonical view.

<a id="s6-p3"></a>[6¶3] `--view=canonical` spells the same view. `--view=decoded` prints the loaded document field by field: section `decoded` (`scope field value`; scope `header`, `row:<key>`, `card:<i>`, `cell:<i>` or `member:<i>`, `i` the 0-based index in canonical order), each row's columns as read plus `value_e6` as the parsed integer and its `unit_code` and `status_code`, then section `item` (`rows values_digest`, the digest recomputed). The decoded view is derived and never an input (§2¶3).

<a id="s6-p4"></a>[6¶4] `--list-measurements` takes no pattern, no `-o`, no `--measures` and no other query.

<a id="s7"></a>
## 7. Failures

<a id="s7-p1"></a>[7¶1] Each of these refuses the compile (or the listing) with a message naming the input:

| failure | where |
|---|---|
| a CR or NUL byte; a row's field count differs from its header's; a row before any header | §2¶1 |
| an unknown section; a derived view's section | §2¶2-¶3 |
| an unknown or repeated header key; a required key missing or empty; `format` not `1`; a bad `id`, `rev`, `tier`, `composite` or `partial` | §2.1 |
| a key breaking the grammar, repeated, of an unknown owner, with no card, or with the wrong token count | §2.3 |
| an unknown unit or status; an empty value on a non-`null` row or a value on a `null` row; a misspelled integer | §2.2¶3, §3.1 |
| a derivation outside §3.2 on a derived or fitted row, or any on a measured or null row; an input that is neither a row nor a cell | §2.2¶3, §3.2 |
| no unit row, or one that is not a `ratio` of `1000000` | §3.1¶2 |
| `rows` or `values_digest` not matching the rows | §3.3¶2 |
| two cards for one quantity; a repeated cell id; `composite` disagreeing with the members | §2.2 |
| a NAME found nowhere; a pinned revision the store lacks; an `-I` file of another id or revision; a shadowing file | §5 |

<a id="s8"></a>
## 8. The store

<a id="s8-p1"></a>[8¶1] The committed sets live in `measure_store/<id>/<rev>/set.tsv`, each with its `PROVENANCE.md`; `measure_store/DEFAULTS` maps each class to its default `id@rev`, and `DEFAULTS.log` records each change of it. A committed revision never changes: a second reading of the same cells is published as a new `rev`, and a new run as a new `id`.

<a id="s8-p2"></a>[8¶2] Every committed set is built into `libpcrec` twice from its one file, as its text and as a pre-parse by the same reader a FILE goes through (`make gen-measures`), so a binary resolves a NAME with no file access and every revision stays selectable from an installed binary.

<a id="s8-p3"></a>[8¶3] Sets today: `zen4-grid1@1` (tier `scratch`, class `x86_64-avx2/zen4`; the `idk` default).
